name: Congenital enteropathy involving intestinal mucosa development

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of abnormal intestinal mucosal development including villous atrophy and epithelial dysplasia
Persistent, severe diarrhea presenting in the neonatal period or early infancy
Exclusion of infectious, metabolic, and immunological causes of enteropathy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in intestinal epithelial development
Evidence of malabsorption and failure to thrive despite adequate nutritional support

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset chronic diarrhea with histopathological confirmation of abnormal intestinal mucosal development and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation and histopathology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Villous atrophy with epithelial dysplasia on intestinal biopsy
searchTerms: damaged intestinal lining with abnormal cells
flattened villi and abnormal gut cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to malabsorption
searchTerms: poor growth from nutrient absorption problems
not gaining weight due to digestion issues

common.symptomName: Electrolyte imbalance secondary to chronic diarrhea
searchTerms: electrolyte problems caused by ongoing diarrhea
salt and mineral imbalance from diarrhea
blood chemistry changes due to diarrhea
mild anemia from poor nutrient absorption
low red blood cells due to digestion issues
heart rhythm problems from electrolyte imbalance
irregular heartbeat due to low minerals

rare.symptomName: Secondary immunodeficiency due to protein loss
searchTerms: weakened immune system from protein loss
immune deficiency due to low blood proteins
increased infection risk from protein deficiency

imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show bowel wall thickening
Radiologic studies may reveal dilated bowel loops
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating intestinal epithelial cell differentiation and mucosal development (e.g., EPCAM, MYO5B)
other: Histopathology showing villous atrophy, epithelial dysplasia, and crypt hyperplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of microvillus inclusions on electron microscopy
Later onset compared to congenital enteropathy

redFlags: Persistent severe diarrhea unresponsive to standard treatment
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutritional support
references: Orphanet: Congenital enteropathy involving intestinal mucosa development, ORPHA:104007
